title: Scrubber Vessel

introduction.definition: A wet scrubber removes pollutants from gas by contact with a liquid. Gas flows up through a packed bed while scrubbing liquor trickles down; acids, dust or odours dissolve or react. A mist eliminator catches droplets before the clean gas leaves.
introduction.summary: A wet scrubber removes acid gases, dust or odours from a gas stream by contact with a scrubbing liquid. Gas flows up through a packed bed while liquor from spray nozzles trickles down over the packing; pollutants dissolve or react in the liquid. A mist eliminator stops droplets leaving with the gas.

video_tutorials.title: Scrubber Vessel — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Scrubber Vessel.
A wet scrubber removes pollutants from gas by contact with a liquid.
Gas flows up through a packed bed while scrubbing liquor trickles down; acids, dust or odours dissolve or react.
A mist eliminator catches droplets before the clean gas leaves.
Typical applications include acid gas removal (HCl, SO₂, NH₃); odour control; process vent treatment; dust removal (venturi/packed).
The cutaway reveals the internal construction.
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

script.narration: How the Scrubber Vessel works.
Dirty gas enters near the bottom.
Liquor is sprayed on top of the packing.
Gas and liquid contact on the packing surface; pollutants transfer to the liquid.
The mist eliminator removes droplets; clean gas exits.
Liquor collects in the sump and is recirculated.

video_tutorials.title: Scrubber Vessel — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Scrubber Vessel.
Check pH, recirculation flow, ΔP.
Clean spray nozzles; check packing.
Replace packing/mist eliminator.
Watch for flooding: high δp, liquid carry-over. Common cause: too much gas or liquid, fouled packing.
Watch for low efficiency: emissions high. Common cause: low ph/flow, blocked nozzles.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
